filename: Machine Learning Workflows in Climate Modeling_ Design Patterns and Insights from Case Studies.pdf
title: Machine Learning Workflows in Climate Modeling: Design Patterns and Insights from Case Studies
parameterization_target: Subgrid atmospheric convection/radiation (ClimSim) and ocean mesoscale eddy subgrid stresses/forcing
testbed_rationale: This paper is a review and methodological synthesis paper presenting design patterns across eight case studies; it does not introduce a standalone dataset or benchmark testbed of its own.
pain_points: Offline performance does not guarantee online stability or physical realism when coupled into host dynamical models.
Coupling Python-based machine learning models with legacy Fortran-based Earth system models requires bridging tools like FTorch and containerized workflows.
Mismatch between differentiable training loss functions (e.g., MSE) and domain metrics of interest (spectral fidelity, conservation laws, decorrelation times, long-term stability).
Severe data sparsity in observational datasets (e.g., surface ocean pCO2 covering only 1-2% of the ocean) leading to extrapolation errors.
Non-stationarity and structural model biases limiting traditional data assimilation and parameter tuning.
Reproducibility issues stemming from inconsistent terminology, lack of standardized workflows, and undocumented design choices.
extraction_notes: The document synthesizes ML workflows across climate modeling into three directions (Physics-First, Data-First, ML-First) and examines eight distinct case studies. It does not present new primary simulation or observational datasets generated by the authors themselves.
